[*]Don't update hidden fields of collapsed work items
[*]Legacy localization loading code was taking 10 seconds on load for no reason

notes.title: Alpha 9.3.1 out on testing branch
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/b5f9ef7abf904d81778b828307fc6326bc55bca6.png[/img]

I still haven't gotten around to balancing contracts and marketing, but there have been huge changes to the simulation balancing overall. Some of these changes will not carry into old saves, as there have been some changes to the software types and AI company types, read more below.

My internet situation seems to have resolved after I permanently switched to LTE and installed network cables in the walls. I went from 300 mbit/s to 100, but oh well.

[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Add finance button to main bottom panel
[*]Save name of each individual bill and show breakdown in company finance window
[*]Toggle between sheet and graph in finance window and have 4 months of backlog instead of 2 months and an average
[*]Printers and pallets should have info when selected
[*]Add stretchable cased opening (doorway with no door) max 3 meters, limited to interior walls
[*]Noise should bleed through walls, where different environments have different levels of background noise, and windows and doors decrease noise isolation depending on wall area
[*]Move audio listener closer to ground
[*]Added support for custom work types in DLL mods
[*]Added ability to check log file and copy to clipboard from main menu
[*]Put print deal income in Deals section of company finances
[*]Add last months product gross column to player releases window
[*]Refund column for player releases
[*]Add team button to contract window
[*]Contract peer reviews should be based on required quality, not actual quality
[*]Sweep selecting an already selected object (ctrl + left mouse drag) will engage sweep deselect mode
[*]Changed marketing costs back to being charged once per day or when done, instead of every second
[/list]

[b]Balancing[/b]
[list]
[*]Made some big changes to sales simulation to increase market interaction, average out sales in each software category, raise the overall average and reduce high selling outliers
[*]The follower mechanic has heavily impacted balancing, so it has been scaled back and is now affected by refunds
[*]Changed how the speed of quality addition is calculated, which greatly impacts the alpha phase
[*]Speed up alpha phase a little
[*]Game engine development has been taken over by AI companies that also make 2D, 3D and audio editors, as they could not make a living on game engines exclusively (Note this won't affect old saves, so your game might be unbalanced if you do not restart)
[*]Reduced game engine development time as it was backing up tech progression(Does not affect old saves)
[*]Chance of picking all features have increased for AI and the chance of picking low feature OSs like phones have decreased to make sure features like 3D aren't unrealistically delayed
[*]Increased average quality of AI company releases
[*]AI companies will try to release software that's missing in the market within their specialization
[*]Improved AI company budget planning to avoid too many bankruptcies and buyouts
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Can't update mods
[*]Fixed scaling of copy order window
[*]Current month for company finance sheet wasn't being updated enough
[*]Marketing budget set in marketing window does not account for currency
[*]Printers should only be on when printing so they don't break suddenly for no reason
[*]Can select wall segments through ground
[*]Room area was not recalculated before lighting propagation when merging rooms causing incorrect indirect lighting between rooms
[*]Fixed bug where framerate would tank if there was unreachable parking spaces
[*]Fixed parking space pathfinding so cars can drive around parked cars
[*]Forgot to remove in-development OS dependency error message when releasing new software for project management 
[*]Replacing a table furniture with a non table furniture was broken and could crash game with infinite loop
[*]Product detail window was missing refund number
[*]Rare chance that AI companies would buy each other out in one move, removing both companies from the game
[*]Employees would try doing alpha work they aren't allowed to because of their role, causing stress and slowdowns
[*]Bankruptcy message needs tweaking and company balance entry should include insurance account to avoid insurance counting as a loss
[*]Clear employee effectiveness stats when they meet, to not give the impression they are still affected by things from last day
[*]Project management action points reset when loading game
[*]Various other bugs
[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list]
[*]Made progress bar a MaskableGraphic instead of having two image components, this also enables gradients
[*]Improved popup duplicate check
[/list]

[*]Fixed employees not taking vacation if sent on education after they went home

[list]
[*]Enumerate employee thoughts, problems and affectors, should not localize them each frame and save to file
[*]Move in-world warning icons from OnGUI to Canvas to increase performance and to have them behind the HUD
[*]Replaced most masks with RectMask2D
[*]Make a IconFillBar and use it to replace the current reputation stars

notes.title: Another alpha 9 progress update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/6d494886023cc8a69df8ba3cbc09e9a56a99a54f.gif[/img]

Hey lovely people! I’m so sorry for the wait.

For the sake of transparency, here’s a breakdown of what’s been going on since the last release status update.

[h1]December[/h1]
As I mentioned in the last update, I moved offices on the 15th of December, which is to say me and my wife moved to a new place, since our lease was up. I don’t actually have a separate office somewhere, I work from home, but it seems appropriate to call it that, given the context.

I was supposed to have an internet connection on the 20th of December, but there was a mix up at the post office, which made the delivery guy send my modem back to the ISP, assuming it was sent to the wrong address. I called the ISP on 3 separate occasions, until I figured out what went wrong and I finally got the modem on the 30th of December. Meanwhile, I’ve been bedridden with a fever for the last couple of weeks of December, so pretty much no work has taken place between my last update and January.

[h1]January[/h1]
I read all your comments while I was sick and panicked. It seems like a lot of you are really hyped for alpha 9, even though I specifically told you I haven’t made huge advancements. What the heck. I scrambled to add new distribution mechanics, so hopefully it doesn’t end up being a big disappointment. I just finished these mechanics, as you can see in the gifs, and I’m basically back to where I was in December: Still need some balancing work and to write reviews for the review generator. I’m already pretty close to finishing the balancing work. Hopefully writing reviews won’t take too long, even though I’m quite bad at it. I’m not going to give an ETA at this point, as that hasn’t worked out for me these last couple of months.

[h1]Distribution overhaul[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/5c8b917ec7e11a72e566c1db37c125a0a2f9cae3.gif[/img]
Having a bunch of separate physical and digital stores has been removed and instead you always sell physical and digital copies of your products. Selling any digital copies in the 80s will be tough, but the market evens out around 2014. You have to actually buy physical copies of your products to sell, or you will only be selling your products digitally. You can buy printers and hire couriers to take over the printing process yourself and possibly earn a little extra by printing for your competitors at a lower price. You can still open an online store to sell your products digitally, but you must make distribution deals with each company separately, taking into account how much of the market you sell to and how big the client is.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
Got really sick + no internet = no work done in December. Panicked about expectations, overhauled and improved distribution mechanic, thereby delaying alpha 9 even further. Alpha 9 shouldn’t be too long now.

notes.title: Alpha 9 progress update
notes.content:
It's now been almost 2 months since the last update. I'd like to say I've made huge advancements, but the truth is these have probably been the slowest months in the development of Software Inc. A lot of non-programming related work has come up during these past months. I'll be moving to a new location on the 15th of December and development should pick up again and be back to full speed from January. The good news is that the amazing support I've received from you has allowed me to work in my company for at least another 4 years, which means I'll be able to finish Software Inc. in good time and start working on a new game as well.

I'm currently done with the bulk of gameplay changes for Alpha 9. There's still a lot of polishing, bug fixes and balancing to be done, before it's ready for release. As always, I'll be doing a testing release initially, to make sure things are relatively balanced and bug free. [b]I'm hoping to have this initial release out before I move to the new location, but if I don't make it before the 15th December, it'll most likely be out in January.[/b]

To make sure you get this release earlier, I've decided to cut some features for the initial release, but I'll make sure to “make room” for the features in the save files, so they'll be out by the time Alpha 9 is done.

[h1]Progress on Alpha 9[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/64e347fd7749672c5472029b64b726990f5734a1.png[/img]
Development no longer works by filling up a progress bar, instead the game now differentiates between code and art progress, and the actual quality of the work done. There's no longer a clear indication of when a product is done, because that doesn't really make sense in the real world and it makes the gameplay a little too simple. To find out how good your product is during development, you'll have to do “peer reviews”, by letting your employees, other companies or clients look over your alpha and rate it.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/09967d7addd79abc8b51dbc8feca1279200c996a.png[/img]
The pre-marketing tasks have been split up and now force you to make timing based decisions. Pre-marketing will attract followers to your product, which represent guaranteed purchases, but you should be vigilant to not lose them again, and make sure you deliver a worthy product, on time. When you product is released, there is no longer a set amount of marketing you have to do each month, instead you'll just have to throw enough employees and money at it, to make sure your product has better exposure than your competitors.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/8c8354944cc64cc98084f6dfebd9b4db851a9f00.png[/img]
Support will now play a bigger role in the game. Support tickets will dynamically follow active user count, there will be no clear indication when support has finished and bugs will have an impact on your sales in the form of refunds.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8600182/649ca086c2980f0c9993412cc67db606f77c3136.png[/img]
Project management has been fixed and completely overhauled. You can have more teams per phase, you can queue up your own projects at will and design and development phases can interleave. There's no longer any education needed and project management tasks are assigned directly to a leader, who must actively work to accumulate “action points” to advance projects.

There's also been a bunch of optimizations, bug fixes and improvements. Notably, you can now develop products for operating systems that are still in development.

[h1]Planned for later releases of Alpha 9[/h1]
The initial release of Alpha 9 will not include these features, but I expect them to be out and compatible with Alpha 9 saves.
[list]
[*]Subsidiaries, which lets you buy out a company without closing them down.
[*]Discounts, the ability to change the price after release and simulate the effects of this.
[*]Individual distribution channels will be removed from the game and replaced with a much simpler system, that will still allow the player to host their own online distribution channel. The player will also have to pay to have physical copies printed of each product.
[*]The ability for the player to print their own or other companies' products, which will involve building product printers and hiring transportation.
[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 8.11.23 out on testing branch
notes.content:
EDIT: Alpha 8.11.23 - Potential fix for employees not leaving at full speed and some other fixes. I expect to release it officially in the next couple of days, then I'll have a new trailer ready and start work on alpha 9.

I've updated Unity to 5.4.

Due to the large amount of different colored furniture the game has to render I developed a solution some months ago, where I combine all furniture into one big object for the graphics card to render all at once. This trades in memory for performance. However, the game has been crashing for some people because the GPU would run out of memory.
Unity 5.4 introduces GPU instancing, which allows me to draw each type of furniture all at once, no matter their color. This might slow performance as all furniture is no longer being drawn at once. If you have a lot of varied furniture from mods, this will be slower, but on the other hand, if you have a lot of similar furniture, like many tables and computers, these will be rendered very quickly. I've traded some performance for stability, but overall the game should still perform a lot better compared to last year.

Note that GPU instancing only works for DirectX11+ and OpenGL 4.1+, if your computer is very old or hasn't been updated for a long time the game might see a big performance hit with a lot of furniture present on screen at once. If your computer is that old it would probably crash out of memory at that point anyway, though.

Since new versions of Unity can prove quite unstable, I'm keeping this in testing for a while to see if the game suddenly stops working for some configurations.

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Road visible from basement after loading game
[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list]
[*]Switch to GPU instancing for furniture
[*]Switch to GPU instancing for cars
[*]Switch to GPU instancing for roads
[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 9 plans and patch release
notes.content:
Here’s a quick patch to fix the most glaring bugs of the last release. Before listing the changelog I’d like to reveal my plans for alpha 9. Note that my plans for alpha 9 might change at any point if something becomes infeasible or doesn’t work well with the rest of the game.

First point of business is the notion of quality. Currently, quality and development duration are synonyms in Software Inc., which doesn’t really make much sense. I plan to separate quality from development progress, such that quality can vary during development, depending on employee skill.

Secondly, I want to get rid of the progressbar in the alpha phase of development. The progressbar mistakenly gave the impression that software should always be outstanding and that releasing early is not a viable strategy. Ideally the average quality of the software you release should be exactly that: “average”. I’m introducing peer reviews instead. You’ll be able to send a build to your employees to test and report back the current state of the product, the accuracy of which will depend on a number of things. I’ll also add “Lines Of Code” and "Art assets" metrics, which will allow you to “learn” when a product is done. But the completeness of a product should not be as apparent as it is now.

Bug count will also be obfuscated. Bugs will impact product success through refunds, and I’m currently debating with myself whether bugs reported through support work should be fixed in separate patch releases, and not directly as it is now.

Pre-marketing is going out and instead you’ll be gaining product followers by utilizing press releases, press builds and going to conferences. Announcing a release date and sticking to it will have positive effects on marketing. Post-marketing will no longer have an upper limit, but you’ll have to actively compete by throwing as much money as possible at marketers and ads.

I’ll be overhauling the newspaper to focus solely on player products and make reviews more detailed.

I’ll make innovation, stability and usability more transparent and give the player complete control over balancing them.

I want to introduce subsidiaries, which will allow you to buy out a company without closing it, and then controlling it, much like automation, but with the added ability to keep in the background and let them do their thing.

[h1]Alpha 8.11.16 changelog:[/h1]
Fixed NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object Company.PayDividends ()

[h1]Alpha 8.11.15 changelog:[/h1]

[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Get stock when buying out company
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]720p doesn't show up in options
[*]Fixed bug in stock valuation when trading stocks, would be based on stock owner value instead of actual company
[/list]

[h1]Alpha 8.11.14 changelog:[/h1]

[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Lowered social needs, now takes twice as long for people to feel isolated
[*]Employees will try to meet at watercooler every 3 hours if they have low social stat, instead of once per day
[*]Removed coffee vapor, not worth the performance cost
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Audience retention was not scaled with days per month
[*]Fixed trying to check feature dependency for features that are not compatible with selected software category. Found by selecting "Fighting" category in "Game" software from mod
[*]Fixed employees sometimes not leaving behind items, so they end up holding on to them forever, breaking their behavior, e.g. not going to the watercooler because they already have water
[/list]

notes.title: New save system in testing branch(Again)
notes.content:
Sorry about my mess up in the last update. Fortunately the faulty update was only out for 1 hour and it appears that at most 7 people were affected. Unfortunately someone had to run into the issue for me to find it. Your save files should still be recoverable by replacing them with the "savefile.sav.bak" version, unless you loaded the game, saved it, exited the game, then loaded it and saved it again.

The save system has been fixed up and I've run some tests that compares every single variable of every single object in a save file, to make sure there are no differences between the old and new save files. This new version also saves an "orig" version of your save file, which is your save file exactly as it was before this update.

If you have any save files from the last update, make sure to revert to the "bak" version.

To switch back to a backup save file, go to the Saves folder where you installed the game, delete the bad save file and remove the ".bak" from the end of the backup version.

[b]Fixes in this version[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed not being able to change List<> variables in furniture mods
[*]Limit company and employee name length
[*]Limit amount of vertices being added to line charts to avoid mesh size error
[/list]

This update has been rolled back to prevent further corrupt save games as the save system is broken. To roll back to your old saves, go to the Saves folder where you installed the game, delete the bad save file and remove the ".bak" from the end of the backup version.

To mitigate this the game will save a backup version in the old format every time you save a game, which you can switch to in the event something goes wrong. This means the game will save two files, which takes up extra space and takes a little more time. You can switch back to the default branch in Steam if you want out.

To switch back to a backup save file, go to the Saves folder where you installed the game, delete the bad save file and remove the ".bak" from the end of the backup version.

[b]Fixes in this version[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed not being able to change List<> variables in furniture mods
[*]Limit company and employee name length
[*]Limit amount of vertices being added to line charts to avoid mesh size error
[/list][/strike]

notes.title: Alpha 8.10 out on testing branch
notes.content:
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/ChTeaser3.gif[/img]
This version might be in testing for awhile as there are many new systems to debug.
All employees in previous saves will have randomized styles to fit the new character model and all fridges will be replaced with vending machines.

Known issues:
Faces turn black on DirectX 9
New version of Unity has increased game size for debugging purposes and they don't plan on changing it. Biggest impact on OSX.

[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Added canteen and cooks
[*]Character model replaced and customization system reworked
[*]Added unofficial support for .NET mods
[*]Update to Unity 5.3.4, should fix NVidia Optimus issues
[*]Ability to change gamma
[*]Censoring on toilet
[*]Improved employee status info in UI with progress bars
[*]OS devtime should not have effect on porting
[*]Only employees talking should increase noise significantly and cubicles should control how much noise an employee makes
[*]Add hint about how more employees do not make development faster
[*]Different types of tasks should have different stress factors
[*]Companies with less than 4 employees shouldn't have to fulfill social needs
[*]Independent employees should be more independent, as their social needs only relate to their working hours
[*]Made it so interaction points can have a minimum requirement, warning appears if less than the minimum is unreachable
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed central heating and AC calculation
[*]Fixed leaders not being social with employees at computers they own
[*]Fixed leaders yoyo-ing between socializing with employees and working for no reason
[*]Fixed bug in how AI companies calculate feature dependencies
[*]Fixed game freezing when there are errors in room edge definitions
[*]Handled case where room edge definition had the same start and ending edge
[*]Fixed game lagging if cleaning staff can't get to a dirty room
[*]Fixed degenerate triangles in navmesh causing buggy paths
[*]Fixed path weighting issues
[*]Work tasks sometimes stop updating
[*]Extend inner walls to outerwall to avoid window see-through
[*]Unavailable furniture should be ignored for room cloning and handled in blueprint info screen
[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list]
[*]Improved performance when wiring server clusters by preserving the largest cluster
[*]Furniture is now combined per floor instead of per room to reduce draw calls
[/list]

[img][/img]

notes.title: Alpha 8.1 out on testing branch
notes.content:
The beta branch has changed name to "testing" to avoid confusion, please switch if you still want to try the broken versions.
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Screen12M12.png[/img]
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Screen4M12.png[/img]
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Screen15M12.png[/img]

[h1]So let's begin with the major features:
[list]
[*]You can now build outdoor areas
[*]You can now research and patent specific features which will allow you to receive royalties
[*]Added new software and new features
[*]Feature selection has been overhauled
[*]You can copy entire furniture arrangements at a time
[*]There is a panel with all details on each furniture in the build menu
[*]You can port software to other operating systems after release
[*]HR management has been improved
[/list][/h1]

Old saves no longer work!

And the full change log:
[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Sequels should have reduced development time depending on shared features + color code shared features in design document
[*]Companies should pay dividends to stock owners
[*]Should be able to limit software types to specific operating system categories
[*]Spread out feature releases so there are constantly new things on the market
[*]Allow for feature to be restricted to multiple categories with individual unlock dates
[*]Assigning an employee to a chair in front of a computer will now automatically assign the computer as well
[*]Improved employee wall and object avoidance
[*]Bugs are easier to fix on contracts to avoid big reputation penalties
[*]Having more teams per project has a chance to slow down development a small bit depending on project size and number of teams
[*]Ability to override software categories for mods and enforce feature order as defined in mod XML
[*]Split furniture painting groups logically, so all wooden tables use the same default color
[*]Add company button to product detail window
[*]You can now use the grid snap tool to snap to the middle of a wall or middle off by one
[*]Added warning bubble to server button when processes are unsupported
[*]Need quality should only affect quality based on the features that depend on it, except for OS needs
[*]Enable click and drag for wide windows
[*]Add server ventilation unit and remove super cooling
[*]Move/Copy multiple pieces of furniture at a time
[*]Added drag camera keybinding
[*]Added floor changing buttons in UI
[*]Do furniture availability check as soon as it is placed by checking all interactionpoints after they've been updated
[*]Allow non forced dependencies on forced features
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed bug causing "Units sold" column to be doubled when loading a game
[*]Fixed saving at exactly the right time causing employees to not spawn
[*]Strictly inside polygon check failed causing furniture to flatten against wall in some situations
[*]Having more teams per projects makes employees work faster
[*]Overriding software features in a mod will now delete the software's base features
[*]Can pick locked categories for autodev
[*]Server deals can now positively affect business reputation
[*]Override walk animation when moving vertically
[*]Increase server usage cutoff before cancelling support
[*]Employees not using their team's meeting time when hired
[*]One corrupt save file would cause the game to skip loading the rest of the save files
[*]Fixed more bugs relating to elevators and splitting/merging rooms
[*]Fixed stretchable segments defaulting to 1m width when moving mouse further than wall length or blockade
[*]Refrigerator can be placed on top of itself multiple times
[*]IP deals should cancel all work deals for the product
[*]Contracts end early with more days per month
[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list]
[*]Switched from Floyd-Warshall to parallelized Breadth First Search implementation and optimized memory allocations to reduce building lag with many rooms present
[*]Cache what meshes should be highlighted when selected and remove debugging code
[*]Fix employee audiosource distance limit
[/list]

Enjoy!

notes.title: Alpha 7.6 on beta branch
notes.content:
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/Screen21M11.png[/img]

This update adds 2 small mini games, which you can use to pass time in the beginning of the game. Otherwise the main focus of this update has been CPU optimizations, mostly in regard to the furniture update loop and overhead when placing buildings and furniture.

I have decided to push back the addition of the statistics window in favor of more important core game mechanics, which have been suggested to me by you over the last couple of weeks, more on that in the next update. 

I plan on releasing one more bug fix update to wrap up alpha 7. A hotfix might be necessary in the meantime, as is usually the case.

[b]Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Added 2 optional mini games to boost design and alpha phase during early game
[*]Marketing should get progressively harder, as you try to reach the remaining consumers, but it should still feel effective in the beginning
[*]Added "Only use own licenses" toggle for project management
[/list]

[b]Fixes[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed employees getting stuck loitering
[*]Fixed accidentally reversing furniture list making employees pick the least favorable piece of furniture to go to first
[*]IP trading was still broken making the player able to earn too much with no reputation
[*]Fixed cars and employees getting stuck if removing road below and then building on top of a car
[*]Staff times still not updating as expected
[*]Reset feature list scroll in design document when chagning type/category
[*]Force minimum wall distance before snapping to keep player from building walls with virtually no space between them
[*]Converted translation files to UTF8 with UNIX line endings as the added lines in alpha 7.6 broke on OSX
[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list]
[*]Optimized tree removal and reduced number of room distance calculations to improve building placement/cloning lag
[*]Only update electricity and water consumption when furniture is turned on and off, instead of all the time (also fixes electricity bills not accumulating when skipping time) Might incur a large bill when loading previous saves
[*]Only update furniture visibility when necessary
[*]Remove expensive null checks in update loop
[*]More rigorous light disabling checks on lower floors
[*]Cache traffic system pathfinding results
[*]Ignore furniture at big distances when fixing navmesh to minimize point to line comparisons, which reduces loading times and furniture and room placement lag
[/list]

notes.content:
Edit:
Hotfix 2:

[*]Button to reset room and furniture to user default style
[*]Fixed bug in pathfinding bug fix

[*]Optimized dropdown list population by caching list elements, as it was causing huge lag, especially when connecting and placing servers
[*]Employee effectiveness calculations are now limited to 1000 times per second(20 employees * 50 frames), since it bottlenecked the CPU pretty hard
[/list]

notes.content:
[b]Older saves no longer work![/b]
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/Screen16M11.png[/img]
This update has focused on updating the underlying market simulation, which means a lot of balancing is needed to get the game back to a playable state. I would love to get feedback on progression and balancing issues regarding sales and reputation.

Changes:
[list]
[*]Software can now be split between categories, like phone, console and PC operating systems (This breaks all mods, I will update the modding wiki soon)
[*]Instead of an overall reputation meter you now have business reputation, fans and market recognition. Market recognition is split between software categories and controls your ability to sell products
[*]Sales are now calculated per unit, instead of just in cashflow, which means user retention and active users are tracked
[*]You can set the price of your product, currently it cannot be changed after it has been chosen, this will change in a future update

[*]Pre-marketing now adds software hype, which makes people hold out on buying current software to buy the hyped products instead
[*]You can prioritize work, by changing it's priority between 1 and 10. The priority number signifies how many extra cycles the employees will work on each work item
[*]Added 90s computer and laptop
[*]All computers can now have extra add-ons such as phones or drawing tablets, which add a boost depending on the type of work the employee is doing
[*]You can rename software while it's in development
[*]Sales vary during the year with more sales around December
[*]Various performance optimizations, and fixes for bugged optimizations, such as furniture material batching
[*]Clouds fade in close proximity to camera to avoid occluding the view
[*]Upgraded main menu picture taking tool
[*]Upgraded ambient occlusion and added Screen Space Reflections(Makes my Geforce GTX 980 Ti struggle with SSAA enabled, so beware)
[*]All sorts of usability fixes and tweening
[/list]

notes.title: Quick update on alpha 7 progress
notes.content:
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/12/Screen14M11.png[/img]
So, I’ve been very quiet since I went full time and as such I wanted to give a quick update on what’s happening. The next update is focused on the market simulation aspect of the game, so there’s not much to show, it’s all code and numbers. The changes I’ve made reach pretty deep, and I’ve managed to break save and mod compatibility and if you had any strategies, they probably won’t work anymore. 

Currently I’ve hidden most of the inconsistent logic in the market simulation behind really abstract math. It’s hard to figure out what’s wrong when you get a “You received $20000 this month”, without any real context. So to change this I’ve switched to calculating actual unit sales, which means I can track active users of each software, actual server bandwidth load, actual user operating system coverage and you can set the price of your software, see exactly how many fans you have, etc.

This also means the simulation has to be a lot more realistic than it is now, which is really hard to get right. On one hand, big operating systems should sell millions of copies and should be priced high and on the other hand companies having trillions of dollars doesn’t make sense gameplay wise. I have to find some middle ground, which means changing some numbers, playing the game for 15 minutes, changing some numbers, playing the game for 15 minutes, changing some numbers, playing the game… You get the point.

Another thing I’m trying to achieve, which has also been requested a lot, is company specialization. Currently, you just try to push out as much software as possible. I’ve changed the reputation system so it’s split between business reputation, for company/employee interactions, and consumer reputation, measured in fans. Company reputation no longer directly affects sales, instead it affects your ability to get market recognition in different software markets, which directly affects sales. This forces you to pick a specialization for your company if you want to survive, and you can start moving into other software markets once you achieve some fame.

This brings me to the final big simulation change: Software categories. Each software type can now be split into categories, e.g. games have RPG, FPS, simulation, etc. Each category has different fan retention rates, development difficulty and popularity, and sometimes features. Once you have broken into a market in, say, RPG games, you will have an easier time breaking into the market for other types of games.

Hopefully, all these changes will make the game a lot more interesting to play. In my short play sessions I can already feel the excitement of seeing the fan number rising, slowly causing more sales.

I’m also adding a 90s computer, which a lot of you requested. It doesn’t really make sense to jump directly from Commodore to flat screen. And as an added bonus: Laptops. I’m planning on adding computer add-on furniture, like tablets and phones, to increase effectiveness of certain employees. Not sure yet if it’ll make it into alpha 7 though.

notes.title: New building mechanic officially released
notes.content:
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/Poster.png[/img]
The new building mechanic is now officially out. And I have two other big announcements, which I will talk about during this month!

[h1]To reiterate:[/h1]
Alpha 5 save games no longer work, you can switch to Alpha 5 in Steam
The price will go up to 14 dollars soon

[h1]Change log from Alpha 5[/h1]
[list]
[*]You can now build rooms in any shape and easily split and merge them
[*]You can build the large window from wall to wall by dragging the mouse
[*]Double doors and wide windows have been added
[*]Hiring and insurance mechanics have been overhauled. You now search for employees by suggesting a salary up front, and you can pre-emptively interview everyone in specific areas
[*]The right click context menu has been upgraded visually and can now be bound to a key in the options menu
[*]The notification area has been upgraded visually to be less intrusive and some notifications can be clicked to highlight a problem
[*]Fixed windows collapsing in on themselves and not working until size was reset in the options menu
[*]Big optimizations for various furniture
[*]Selected object can now be seen through other objects
[*]Cars no longer wait for employees through walls
[*]Deleting a basement with employees in it would break the employees
[*]Meeting tables no longer need to be stacked next to each other, to be used as meeting tables
[*]Competitors will release better quality software on average above easy mode
[*]Newer computers are actually faster
[*]You can delete saves from the save game window
[*]You can re-enable the marketing dialog that appears when releasing software, in the options window
[*]Employees will no longer work on support if there are no tickets in queue
[*]Building, hiring and insurance tutorials have been updated
[/list]

Alpha 7 will focus on gameplay, with features such as more teams per project, manually setting product price, more stats and improved heating/cooling system.

Cars no longer hold for employees that are inside buildings

notes.title: New build system being developed
notes.content:
Watch the prototype in action:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2A987YiYxCc

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
[list]
[*]New build system means you can build rooms in any shape
[*]Next official update might take a couple of months, beta probably within a month
[*]Game will cost $14 when next official update releases
[/list]

[h1]All the juicy details[/h1]
You might recall from the latest patch notes that I would try revamping the build system, and if you’ve followed me on twitter ( https://twitter.com/SoftwareIncGame ), you will know that my attempt has been successful.

I have finished a working prototype and I will be spending the next weeks replacing the current build system in Software Inc. with the new system. There is a lot of code to replace and a lot of stuff will no longer work, like the dirt system, so it might take a while. 

The biggest hurdle, however, will be completely re-implementing pathfinding. To get it out of the door and get it tested as quickly as possible, I will release a version on the beta branch with broken pathfinding, which means everything will work, but employees will go straight to their destination through furniture and in some cases through walls. This way you can try it out and I might get some bugs fixed, while I finish the pathfinding system up. I expect the first release to happen in about 2-6 weeks.

This will of course push back what I had planned for alpha 6 to alpha 7. It’s important to note that this is an increase in the scope of the game, I will not slack off on the management aspect of the game. This addition will add to the development time of Software Inc., not take away from it. This also means that the final price of Software Inc. will go up $2, and it will increase to $14 when the new build system is released publically. This is in addition to the price increase I already had panned, which means it might go up to $16 when alpha 7 is done.

Some details about the new build system:
[list]
[*]You can now place walls individually, instead of a rectangle at a time, but walls have to be connected, you can’t have walls to nowhere like the Sims
[*]The grid is no longer forced, you can build however you want, I’ve put in some constraints on angles and sizes so it doesn’t break completely, like paper thin rooms
[*]Furniture can be placed anywhere and have any size and shape
[*]Doors and windows can be placed anywhere, as it slides along the wall when you place it, and it can now have any size, which allows for stuff like double doors
[*]You can split rooms by simply drawing a wall through them
[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 5.4 out in beta
notes.content:
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/Screen4M10.png[/img]
We're nearing the ending of Alpha 5, the only thing missing is paying for server bandwidth from a competitor.

[*]Fixed the new OS product influence calculation causing OSs to sell way past their due date at ludicrous amounts

[*]Made weather parameters interchangeable and adjusted overall temperature
[*]Added desert, tundra, and cactus trees
[*]Furniture now keeps their employee assignment when upgrading
[*]Added a window detailing all announced product releases from AI companies
[*]Build menu categories can now only have one be selected or everything selected
[*]Enabled making sequels for project management
[*]Fixed not being able to cancel support deal after working on it
[*]Auto development post marketing is now handled automatically and hidden from player
[*]Added a window that details current work and project information for automation projects
[*]Fixed selected items in a list not persisting when the items in the list changed
[*]Fixed list content hiding to the left when scaling window to the right
[/list]

You can currently pick between Forest (the one you're used to) and City (with procedurally generated roads and skyscrapers). The city is still work in progress, the only difference currently is that you get a finished road system and parking as you expand without the need to build it yourself. I also want to add a desert setting in the future.

Changelog:
[list]
[*]Fixed game breaking when cloning a room in which a computer was bought before the table it is currently placed upon, including tables that were upgraded
[*]Balanced development time/team size
[*]Feature dependency should take hierarchy into consideration, e.g. music editor for audio tool should be available with HD audio, not just 8 bit audio
[*]Sped up animation to alleviate employees breaking at fastest speed
[*]Added procedurally generated skyscrapers and road to city mode
[/list]

notes.title: Small difficulty update
notes.content:
A lot of you have been reporting that the game has gotten too hard in the last update, so I made Easy mode a lot easier. Medium difficulty is also a bit easier now, but hard mode stays the same (hard mode is currently the base line I work off of).

Lowering difficulty will increase sales, work speed and base skill effect, so 0%-100% skill will actually be 25%-100% behind the scenes on easy mode.

This is very small "hack" to alleviate the problems I introduced with the last alpha release. I'll be digging deeper into the problem in the weekend, before I start work on Alpha 5.

You might need to restart Steam in order to get the update.

notes.title: Alpha 4.7 released in beta
notes.content:
The calculation of how much development time a product will take has been completely revamped, which has made the game more realistic and, as such, a bit harder. I have made the difficulty settings have a bigger effect on development time to alleviate this.

As with Alpha 4.6, if this release does not have too many glaring bugs, this will mark the end of Alpha 4.

Change log:
[list]
[*]More intelligent OS and needs picking for auto dev and AI companies
[*]New optimal employee count calculation and rebalancing of dev times and dev speed
[*]Limited how far necks can turn during meetings to below The Exorcist levels
[*]Difficulty setting now affects development time
[*]Removed ability to take products off market as it didn’t really serve a purpose anymore
[*]Fixed specialization skill resetting to base skill after education (The infamous skills decreases over time problem)
[*]Product perception is now calculated as quality/(maximum quality on market) instead of quality/(average quality on market) fixing a lot of weird market behavior
[*]Software size is now considered relative to what is available on the market, e.g. text based games will sell a lot of copies before 2D is introduced
[*]Each OS supported outside of the first one now extends development time by a month
[*]Added warning icons above unreachable furniture
[*]Added warning icons when parking spot is unreachable
[*]Added warning icons when employees can’t get home
[*]Putting something on a wall, then deleting it and then splitting/merging/expanding the room would cause the game to break and making the player unable to save
[*]Raised minimum reputation from 0.001% to 0.1%
[*]Fixed employees not prioritizing furniture by room distance first
[*]Fixed interest from insurance account not being equal to what was reported
[*]Game breaks if employee has been fired while driving to work
[*]Salary negotiation will be forced after hiring someone or changing their roles
[*]Fixed code/art work ratio during alpha development being completely wrong
[*]Employees are now willing to park an arbitrary distance from their office
[*]Added warning when cloning large amounts of stuff
[*]Optimized cloning several rooms at once (only rebuild pathing and meshes when all rooms have been cloned)
[*]Fixed list sorting being unstable
[*]Fixed employees preferring unused table groups when loitering (would end up reserving all tables for no reason)
[*] “Select furniture in selected rooms” will now select the selected furniture types in all selected rooms or all furniture if only rooms are selected
[*]You can now place furniture which hang on walls in corners next to each other
[*]Fixed temporary IT staff not going home when all work is done
[*]Disabled hunger and bladder need during meetings
[*]Fixed some furniture not keeping color after room cloning
[*]Unlit rooms are no longer completely black
[*]Moving couch caused wrong grid tiles to be made unwalkable
[*]Couches not deleted when room splits it
[*]Mostly fixed employees sometimes taking the long route if it means walking outside
[*]Fixed elevator being cloned twice with cloning tool
[*]Various bugs that would crash the game
[/list]

notes.content:
This update is currently only on the beta branch.

This update mostly features bug fixes. I've been pretty backed up this last week, so progress is moving a little slow right now, but it should pick up during June/July.
As always, I'll keep an eye out for feedback tagged Alpha 4.5 and release it officially before this Wednesday.

I'm keeping a new change log, outside of the official bugtracker and Trello board, which includes all the "small" stuff, so that I can release a more detailed change log. So without further ado. Changes in Alpha 4.5:

[*]Turning furniture didn’t update whether it could be placed properly
[*]Roads and rooms are now more expensive
[*]Fixed cars not being affected by volume settings
[*]Project management was broken after a release with no bugs
[*]Collapsed vacation notifications into one notification
[*]Vacation should happen more often when days per month > 1
[*]Furniture break timer should have some randomization
[*]Fixed employees trying to get coffee making them micro sleep all the time
[*]Added temporary solution for Linux open/shutdown bug 
[*]Adding more employees to a project will no longer increase effectiveness indefinitely
[*]Fixed employees reserving computers owned by other employees, disabling both from using it
[*]Changed how popularity boosts from sequels are calculated
[*]Show simulation progress when starting a new game
[/list]

notes.title: Alpha 4.3 on the beta branch
notes.content:
[img]http://softwareinc.coredumping.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/Screen23M8.png[/img]
[h1]Days per month[/h1]
You can now choose up to 8 days per month and old save files that worked in the last update should still work properly in this update. Note that you can't change this during a game, you have to decide how long you want a month to be when you start a new game. Please post in the forums if you find that something is unbalanced when playing anything other than 1 day per month.

[h1]Employees getting stuck[/h1]
The pathfinding system has been fixed. So employees will no longer get stuck for no reason, so if your employees are still getting stuck, you probably forgot to add a door or an elevator somewhere.

[h1]Corrupted save files[/h1]
A lot of bugs have been fixed in the load mechanism, so if you have some corrupted save files, they probably work now. Otherwise, please send your file to SoftwareInc@Coredumping.com

[h1]Localization[/h1]
I fixed some errors in the localization files, e.g. delay and alpha being switched. For translators: Each update will add a new tag to the bottom of the UI.xml file with the name of the alpha version in which new translations have been introduced. So you can just copy these xml tags to the bottom of the XML files you have now and everything should be accounted for.

I also added a couple of room patterns for good measure, illustrated in the picture above.

Contract countdown starting as soon as you accept it
Leaders holding meetings by themselves
Animation speed slowing down employees when fast forwarding
Shadow banding on the ground at sharp angles

[h1]Changes include:[/h1]
Ability to move furniture
More info in the contract window + more info while working a contract
Taller construction menu
More warnings and tips
Unused founder colors have been removed from the New Game screen
Older notifications are removed instantly to make room for new notifications
You can now distinguish between art and programming work when hovering over an alpha work item
Employees have gotten a little smarter in regards to pathfinding. They will no longer get stumped if they can't go somewhere, because it required them to move through another team's room.

[h1]Time[/h1]
Finally, one thing I've heard a lot of criticism over, is the fact that 1 day = 1 month. I've been thinking about this and I think it's doable. The new system would be 1 day = 1 week, 1 month = 4 weeks. There are some things to consider, and I don't think it'll unambiguously make the game better.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
Slower progression, for people who feel everything is moving too fast
Being able to calculate sales, marketing and reputation 4 times before deducting salaries and bills

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
The game will take four times as long as it does now. 1 year at full fast forwarding will take 40 minutes rather than the current 10 minutes. Developing an Operating System will be a 2 hour endeavor at the very least.
It will push back the current features planned for the next alpha, i.e. crowdfunding campaigns, consumer hype/patience and employee fame.

So please, tell me whether you think 4 day months is a good idea or why it might be worth it.

notes.title: Post Steam patch release
notes.content:
I've fixed all the bugs, which have been reported since Software Inc. released on Steam, and added some usability stuff.

Fixes includes:
The game would freeze in certain situations when cleaning staff were stuck
Inability to get around if a door was blocked off by furniture
Employees not arriving to work
Radiators and other wall furniture being destroyed on room split/merge/expand
Employees being stuck in rooms and not being able to go home due to room team designation
Fixed mouse getting stuck in fly cam mode if modal windows popped up
Fixed bug with fixing bugs (inception stuff going on here) and releasing finished products

Changes include:
Rooms lighting up in build mode to signify lamp lighting
Popups are now hidden in build mode

The only outstanding problem as of now, is that the game is behaving weird and is unplayable on certain Linux installations.

Going forward, new releases will be posted to the beta branch on Steam, which you can opt-in to by right clicking on the game in your Steam library, going to Properties -> Betas and selecting "beta" from the drop-down. You will get to try out new features as they are released, but it might be somewhat unstable and save games might break more often. Bug reports from the beta branch will be fixed and everything will be released on the main branch. If nobody ends up using the beta branch, new updates will go directly to the main branch. The offline version will be permanently in "beta" mode, since you can control how often to download new releases yourself.

Future plans can be viewed on [url=trello.com/b/9I286Mhu/software-inc]Trello[/url]
